title: Seek registration in Queensland before working there on an interstate licence
what: A worker licensed for an occupation in another state must lodge a mutual recognition notice with the Queensland registration authority before working in that occupation in Queensland. Queensland has not adopted automatic deemed registration, so the licence from the home state does not carry over on its own.

sources.title: Mutual Recognition Act 1992 (Cth)
sources.quote: 19 Notification to local registration authority (1) A person who is registered in the first State for an occupation that is equivalent to an occupation in the second State may lodge a written notice with the local registration authority of the second State for the equivalent occupation, seeking registration for the equivalent occupation in accordance with the mutual recognition principle.

sources.title: Mutual Recognition Act 1992 (Cth)
sources.quote: Effect of amendments to this Act on pre-adoption States (3) Despite subsections (1) and (2), the amendments of this Act made by the Mutual Recognition Amendment Act 2021 do not apply to a pre-adoption State.

sources.title: Mutual Recognition Act 1992 (Cth)
sources.locator: s 4 (definition of pre-adoption State) (compilation C2026C00472 from 2026-10-07)
sources.quote: pre-adoption State means a State (other than a Territory) that is a participating jurisdiction, but which has not done either of the following: (a) before the enactment of the Mutual Recognition Amendment Act 2021, referred the mutual recognition matters to the Parliament of the Commonwealth to the extent of the making of laws with respect to those matters by making express amendments to this Act; (b) adopted this Act, as amended by the Mutual Recognition Amendment Act 2021.

sources.title: Mutual Recognition Act 1992 (Cth)
sources.quote: References to States (3) A reference in this Part to a State does not include a reference to a pre-adoption State, unless the expression “any State” is used.

sources.title: Mutual Recognition Act 1992 (Cth)
sources.quote: 25 Interim deemed registration (1) A person who lodges a notice in accordance with section 19 with a local registration authority of a State is, pending the grant or refusal of registration in accordance with Division 2, taken to be registered as provided in section 20.

sources.title: Mutual Recognition (Queensland) Act 1992 (Qld)
sources.quote: (b) the amendment of that Act, but only in terms which are approved by the designated person for each of the then participating jurisdictions.

administration.who: Local registration authorities (occupational regulators in each state)

sources.title: Mutual Recognition Act 1992 (Cth)
sources.locator: s 4, words naming the body (found 18 Nov 2026) (compilation C2026C00472 from 2026-10-07)
sources.quote: local registration authority of a State for an occupation means the person or authority in the State having the function conferred by legislation of registering persons in connection with their carrying on that occupation in the State. Note: Local registration authorities are given additional functions under this Act.

triggers.note: Before working in Queensland on a registration from another state. Once the notice is lodged, the worker is taken to be registered while the authority decides (s 25).

confidence_note: Neither Act names Queensland as a pre-adoption State. That Queensland is one is read from the Commonwealth Act's definition and the Queensland Act, which adopts no amendment made by the Mutual Recognition Amendment Act 2021 (searched 17 November 2026; a 2024 Queensland regulation approves only the change to the Administrative Review Tribunal).

assessment.summary: Queensland stays out of automatic mutual recognition, so licensed workers moving into or out of the state still apply and pay for a separate registration.

marks.reason: Keeps the application and fee licensed workers face when moving between Queensland and other states.
Keeps Queensland's licensed services market separate from the scheme the other states share.
